editorNote: A quiet week of firsts and checkups: a galaxy-survey telescope stumbles onto a comet, Orion's heat shield gets its report card, and a rideshare rocket carries a crowd of small spacecraft.

stories.headline: Euclid finds its first comet, C/2026 S1, while hunting for galaxies
stories.summary: ESA's Euclid telescope turned up a comet in images taken Sept. 16–24; University of Helsinki PhD student Mikko Pöntinen's software flagged a streak, and it sits about 1.3 billion km away with a fuzzy cloud suggesting it is shedding dust and gas.
stories.whyItMatters: Euclid is built to study distant galaxies and avoids the planetary plane where most comets lie, so a comet discovery is a surprise; it is not a fit for ESA's Comet Interceptor but offers a test of how the teams would coordinate.

sourceLinks.title: ESA's Euclid Space Telescope Discovers Its First Comet - Sci.News

stories.headline: NASA says Artemis II's heat shield performed as expected, with 9 char-loss spots versus 103 on Artemis I
stories.summary: After Navy diver imagery, inspections and X-ray scans, NASA says Orion's heat shield matched pre-flight predictions at about 39 times the speed of sound and above 4,000°F outside. A shorter downrange trajectory cut cracking and char loss roughly tenfold.
stories.whyItMatters: The Artemis I heat shield problem was handled by changing the entry path, not the hardware; Artemis III upgrades aim for more uniform Avcoat permeability, with NASA planning an Artemis IV lunar landing in 2028.

sourceLinks.title: Rigorous Analysis Confirms NASA's Artemis II Heat Shield Performance - NASA

stories.headline: Falcon 9 launches Bandwagon-5: SpaceX's Starfall capsule, Varda W-7 and 30 other payloads
stories.summary: After a weather scrub on Oct. 19, SpaceX launched the rideshare on Oct. 20 from Cape Canaveral with 32 payloads, including Starfall, a Varda capsule carrying a cancer-drug experiment, and Portal Space Systems' 260 kg Starburst-1.
stories.whyItMatters: It is Starfall's second flight; per an FAA assessment the capsule is about 3.1 m wide and can carry up to 1,000 kg of payload, though SpaceX did not say what it carried this time.
